tagline: Sugarhouses, Amish fields and the quietest highway in New York.
intro: Route 812 leaves Lowville along the Black River, crosses it at New Bremen and goes north through Croghan, Harrisville and Gouverneur, keeping beside the west branch of the Oswegatchie for a while, to De Kalb and Ogdensburg on the St. Lawrence. An alternate loop runs by way of Canton.

NYSDOT's account of the road has family sugar bushes making syrup over wood-stoked fires with horse-drawn wagons, and Amish farmers working their fields. A GPS company has named 812 the quietest highway in the state.

moments.title: Croghan
moments.text: In Croghan, said Krō-gun, the American Maple Museum occupies a school built with money from the estate of Theodore Basselin, the logger who was the town's first millionaire.

moments.title: Heuvelton
moments.text: The village on the Oswegatchie was Fordsburgh until 1832, when it took the name of Jacob Van den Heuvel, a Dutch immigrant who paid for its mills and other improvements.

moments.title: Ogdensburg–Prescott International Bridge
moments.text: The road ends at the foot of a suspension bridge to Canada, finished in 1960 to replace the boats that had crossed between Ogdensburg and Prescott since 1800.
